findings.issue_text: project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:110 — zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes nodestore.get_multi returns results in request order; the dict is unordered so titles/messages can be attributed to the wrong error ID. Look up each event by its node id instead.

project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:151 — Error timestamps are in epoch seconds while rrweb replay events use epoch milliseconds, so the < comparison mixes units and all errors are emitted before the first breadcrumb instead of interleaved chronologically. Normalize units.
browser_reporting_collector.py:51 — validate_timestamp/validate_age use truthiness checks, so age: 0 alongside timestamp bypasses the mutual-exclusion check. Use 'in' / 'is not None' checks.

browser_reporting_collector.py:43 — Both age and timestamp are required=False and nothing enforces at least one is present, so a report with neither validates successfully. Add an object-level validate().

browser_reporting_collector.py:109 — One invalid report in a batch causes a 422 for the whole array, dropping all valid reports; browsers don't retry on 4xx so data is lost. Skip/log bad reports and process the rest.

commit_context.py:587 — get_environment_info calls issue.get_recommended_event() per issue (Snuba query plus nodestore fetch each), adding serial external calls on the merged-PR comment path. Batch the query or fetch only environment from the latest event.

project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:83 — error_ids is read from a response filtered by the caller's field query params; if the caller passes a field list without error_ids, error context silently disappears. Request error_ids explicitly.
project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:136 — get_request_data sorts error_events in place, mutating caller-owned data shared via functools.partial; use sorted() instead.
organization_preprod_artifact_assemble.py:81 — analytics.record fires before the feature-flag check, emitting analytics for orgs rejected with 403. Move it after the gate.

0917_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views.py:14 — Rewriting already-numbered migrations 0917 and 0920 to no-ops relies on the unverified claim they were never run, and references 0921_..._rerevised.py which isn't in the diff; if either was applied anywhere, migration history diverges. Confirm 0921 exists and document state.

commit_context.py:143 — MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE now ends with a newline while callers still join with '\n', producing blank lines between every issue in the rendered comment. Drop the trailing newline.

project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py — No tests for fetch_error_details, the interleaving in gen_request_data, or the enable_error_context=false path; a simple interleave test would have caught the ordering/unit bugs.

goldens.comment: The BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns HttpResponse objects but the endpoint inherits from Endpoint which expects rest_framework.response.Response objects.
In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').

Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).
Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.

Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.

Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:151 — Error timestamps are in epoch seconds while rrweb replay events use epoch milliseconds, so the < comparison mixes units and all errors are emitted before the first breadcrumb instead of interleaved chronologically. adjudication.rationale: The provided diff snippet for `project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py` is truncated well before any logic that compares error timestamps to rrweb/breadcrumb timestamps. While it introduces an `ErrorEvent` TypedDict with a `timestamp: float` and begins fetching replay instance data, there is no visible `<` comparison or any unit conversion/assumption in the shown changes. Therefore the claim about mixing epoch seconds vs milliseconds is not verifiable from the diff provided.

adjudication_records.issue_text: browser_reporting_collector.py:51 — validate_timestamp/validate_age use truthiness checks, so age: 0 alongside timestamp bypasses the mutual-exclusion check. Use 'in' / 'is not None' checks.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `BrowserReportSerializer`, mutual exclusion between `age` and `timestamp` is enforced via `self.initial_data.get("age")` and `self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`. Because `dict.get()` returns the value and the code checks truthiness, providing `age: 0` (or `timestamp: 0`) will be treated as absent and will not trigger the ValidationError, allowing both fields to coexist and bypassing the intended exclusivity. This is directly verifiable from the diff in `validate_timestamp`/`validate_age`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: browser_reporting_collector.py:43 — Both age and timestamp are required=False and nothing enforces at least one is present, so a report with neither validates successfully. Add an object-level validate().

adjudication.rationale: In BrowserReportSerializer, both `age` and `timestamp` are declared `required=False`. The only enforcement is via `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age`, which only run when their respective fields are present. If a report includes neither `age` nor `timestamp`, no validator triggers and the serializer will still consider the data valid. Given the comment that the endpoint must support two specs with non-overlapping fields, it should enforce that at least one of (`age`, `timestamp`) is provided (typically via an object-level `validate`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: browser_reporting_collector.py:109 — One invalid report in a batch causes a 422 for the whole array, dropping all valid reports; browsers don't retry on 4xx so data is lost. Skip/log bad reports and process the rest.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does make the endpoint return HTTP 422 immediately on the first invalid item in the `raw_data` array (`if not serializer.is_valid(): ... return Response(..., status=422)`), so valid reports later in the batch are not processed. However, whether that is a “real problem” is not verifiable from the diff: rejecting the entire request on any invalid element can be an intentional API/validation choice, and the claim that “browsers don't retry on 4xx so data is lost” depends on external browser/spec behavior not shown or enforced in this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: commit_context.py:587 — get_environment_info calls issue.get_recommended_event() per issue (Snuba query plus nodestore fetch each), adding serial external calls on the merged-PR comment path. Batch the query or fetch only environment from the latest event.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `CommitContextIntegration.get_environment_info()`, which calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` for each issue. Both GitHub and GitLab PR comment workflows were changed to call `get_environment_info(issue)` inside the per-issue list comprehension that builds the merged-PR comment body. This creates an N-per-issue event lookup on the PR-comment path (previously it only used already-available fields like `issue.culprit`). While the exact underlying storage (Snuba/nodestore) isn’t shown in the diff, the added per-issue recommended-event fetch is verifiable and can reasonably introduce serial external I/O / latency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:83 — error_ids is read from a response filtered by the caller's field query params; if the caller passes a field list without error_ids, error context silently disappears. Request error_ids explicitly.

adjudication.rationale: In the shown diff chunk, `query_replay_instance(...)` is called without any field list, and the only place the caller’s `field` query params are used is as an argument to `process_raw_response(snuba_response, fields=request.query_params.getlist("field"), ...)`. The diff excerpt does not show any subsequent code reading `error_ids` (or relying on it) from the processed/filtered response, so the claim that `error_ids` “silently disappears” is not directly verifiable from the provided diff and depends on unseen code/behavior of `process_raw_response` and later logic.

While `functools` is imported, the proposed finding’s specific claim (line 136, `get_request_data` sorting `error_events` in place and mutating caller-owned data via `functools.partial`) is not verifiable from the provided diff content. adjudication_records.issue_text: 0917_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views.py:14 — Rewriting already-numbered migrations 0917 and 0920 to no-ops relies on the unverified claim they were never run, and references 0921_..._rerevised.py which isn't in the diff; if either was applied anywhere, migration history diverges. Confirm 0921 exists and document state.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly rewrites two already-numbered Django data migrations (0917 and 0920) from performing a SavedSearch->GroupSearchView conversion into unconditional no-ops (`return`) while asserting in comments they “were never run” and pointing to a “0921_..._rerevised.py” as the correct replacement. Modifying historical migrations like this can cause correctness issues if these migrations were applied in any environment (migration history divergence / missing data conversion), and the diff itself provides no verification of the claim or inclusion of the referenced corrective migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: commit_context.py:143 — MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE now ends with a newline while callers still join with '\n', producing blank lines between every issue in the rendered comment. Drop the trailing newline.

adjudication.rationale:
The diff introduces `MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE = "* ‼️ [**{title}**]({url}){environment}
"` in `commit_context.py`, i.e. each rendered issue line already ends with a newline. In both `github/integration.py` and `gitlab/integration.py`, the issue list is still built via `"
".join([ self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...) for issue in issues ])`. Joining strings that already end with `
` using an additional `
` separator will produce `

` between items, yielding blank lines between every issue in the rendered comment. Dropping the trailing newline (or changing the join logic) would fix it.
